rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After 42:3 exalts revelation to Muhammad and earlier prophets, this verse details that shared divine legislation.
rows.anchor: لما عظم وحيه إلى محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم بقوله { كذلك يوحى إليك وإلى الذين من قبلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed Muhammad's community the religion He enjoined on Noah, Muhammad, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus.
rows.anchor: شرع الله لكم يا أصحاب محمد من الدين ما وصى به نوحا ومحمدا وآبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These five are singled out because they are the leading prophets, bearers of great laws, and followed by many.
rows.anchor: لأنهم أكابر الأنبياء وأصحاب الشرائع العظيمة والأتباع الكثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi flags the differing formulas for Noah, Muhammad, and Abraham as a textual problem requiring explanation.
rows.anchor: أنه قال في أول الآية { ما وصى به نوحا } وفي آخرها { وما وصينا به إبراهيم } وفي الوسط { والذى أوحينا إليك } فما الفائدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He also asks why Noah is described in the third person while the references to Muhammad and Abraham use the first person.
rows.anchor: أنه ذكر نوحا عليه السلام على سبيل الغيبة فقال : { ما وصى به نوحا } والقسمين الباقيين على سبيل التكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further difficulty is the apparent shift from third-person address in “He prescribed” to direct address in “We revealed to you” within one construction.
rows.anchor: فهذا يقتضي الجمع بين خطاب الغيبة وخطاب الحضور في الكلام الواحد بالاعتبار الواحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common religion means unchanging beliefs in God, angels, books, messengers, and the Last Day, not legal rules that vary by community; it calls for turning from worldly life, seeking the afterlife, virtue, and avoiding vice.
rows.anchor: الأمور التي لا تختلف باختلاف الشرائع / وهي الإيمان بالله وملائكته وكتبه ورسله واليوم الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi proposes that the prohibition on division may mean rejecting numerous gods, as Joseph calls people divided among gods inferior to worshipping the One, and messengers preach that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: ويجوز عندي أن يكون المراد من قوله { ولا تتفرقوا } أي لا تتفرقوا بالآلهة الكثيرة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some infer that Muhammad initially followed Noah's law; Razi rejects this, since the verse also names other prophets and points to the law agreed upon by them all.
rows.anchor: واحتج بعضهم بقوله { شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا } على أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to establish religion can be parsed as an accusative substitute for the object of “prescribed” and its coordinated clauses, or as a nominative resumption answering what was prescribed.
rows.anchor: إما نصب بدل من مفعول

words: كَبُرَ عَلَى ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ مَا تَدْعُوهُمْ إِلَيْهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The call to establish God's religion in agreement and unanimity was grave and difficult for the polytheists.
rows.anchor: عظم عليهم وشق عليهم { ما تدعوهم إليه } من إقامة دين الله تعالى على سبيل الاتفاق والإجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists' complaint that Muhammad would make many gods into one illustrates why this call was hard for them.
rows.anchor: بدليل أن الكفار قالوا { أجعل الالهة إلاها واحدا إن هاذا لشىء عجاب }

rows.speaker: نفاة القياس
rows.claim: Opponents of analogical reasoning argue that the command to establish one religion without division forbids qiyas, since it opens the door to disputes and schools based on it remain divided through the end of time.
rows.anchor: احتج نفاة القياس بهذه الآية قالوا إنه تعالى أخبر أن أكابر الأنبياء أطبقوا على أنه يجب إقامة الدين بحث لا يفضي إلى الاختلاف والتنازع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Religious prescriptions include permanent principles that cannot be abrogated, such as truthfulness, justice, and beneficence, and variable rules that differ among religions, such as prohibitions of lying, oppression, and harm.
rows.anchor: منها ما يمتنع دخول النسخ والتغيير فيه ، بل يكون واجب البقاء في جميع الشرائع والأديان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The law gives stronger emphasis to the permanent moral principles because observing them cultivates states that bring happiness in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: ودلت هذه الآية على أن سعي الشرع في تقرير النوع الأول أقوى من سعيه في تقرير النوع الثاني

words: أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Agreement is valued by both reason and revelation because aligned souls strengthen one another's influence.
rows.anchor: أن للنفوس تأثيرات ، وإذا تطابقت النفوس وتوافقت على واحد قوي التأثير

words: أَنْ أَقِيمُوا۟ ٱلدِّينَ وَلَا تَتَفَرَّقُوا۟ فِيهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Agreement lets each person assist the others toward a shared aim, and more helpers make success more likely.
rows.anchor: أنها إذا توافقت صار كل واحد منها معينا للآخر في ذلك المقصود المعين ، وكثرة الأعوان توجب حصول المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disagreement undermines the world's welfare by producing disorder, killing, and plunder; the same principle appears in the prohibition on contention in 8:46.
rows.anchor: حصول التنازع ضد مصلحة العالم لأن ذلك يفضي إلى الهرج والمرج والقتل والنهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is that God directed Muhammad's community to the shared religion because He chose them and singled them out for added mercy and honor.
rows.anchor: إلى التمسك بالدين المتفق عليه بين أنه تعالى إنما أرشدهم إلى هذا الخير ، لأنه اجتباهم واصطفاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that the messengers' call was hard for the polytheists because obedience to them wounded their pride; God chooses messengers regardless of rank, lineage, or wealth, and people must follow them.
rows.anchor: من الانقياد لهم تكبرا وأنفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ijtabā derives from gathering and drawing something together, as in collecting revenue or gathering water in a basin; God's choosing means drawing someone near with honor and mercy.
rows.anchor: واشتقاق لفظ الاجتباء يدل على الضم والجمع ، فمنه جبي الخراج واجتباه وجبى الماء في الحوض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “whomever He wills” follows the pattern of 29:21, where God says He punishes and shows mercy to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: يعذب من يشاء ويرحم من يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported divine saying promises that whoever approaches God by obedience receives God's approach through guidance, the opening of the heart, and ease in affairs.
rows.anchor: الخبر ( من تقرب مني شبرا تقربت منه ذراعا ومن أتاني يمشي أتيته هرولة )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning to God brings His guidance and direction: He opens the servant's heart and makes the path easier.
rows.anchor: من أقبل إلي بطاعته أقبلت إليه بهدايتي وإرشادي بأن أشرح له صدره وأسهل أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier communities divided only after learning that division was error; envy, the pursuit of leadership, ego, and pride drove each faction to promote its own doctrine and denigrate others.
rows.anchor: أنهم ما تفرقوا إلا من بعد أن علموا أن الفرقة ضلالة ، ولكنهم فعلوا ذلك للبغي وطلب الرياسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who split deserved punishment, but God postponed it to an appointed term, either by sheer will (Razi's view) or because postponement was beneficial (the Muʿtazilite view).
rows.anchor: إما لمحض المشيئة كما هو قولنا ، أو لأنه علم أن الصلاح تحقيقه به كما عند المعتزلة

rows.speaker: الأكثرون
rows.claim: Most commentators identify those who divided after receiving knowledge as the Jews and Christians, supported by 3:19 and 98:4.
rows.anchor: فقال الأكثرون هم اليهود والنصارى ، والدليل قوله تعالى في آل عمران

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Others identify them as the Arabs, but Razi rejects this: the following reference to people inheriting scripture fits the People of the Book, not the Arabs.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون : إنهم هم العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who inherited scripture after the earlier disputants are the People of the Book contemporary with Muhammad; they remain in troubling doubt about their own book and do not truly believe it.
rows.anchor: لأن الذين أورثوا الكتاب من بعدهم ، هم أهل الكتاب الذين كانوا في عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people who dispute about God after people have accepted the religion are arguing over His religion after others have responded to it.
rows.anchor: والذين يحاجون في الله } أي يخاصمون في دينه { من بعد ما استجيب له } أي من بعد ما استجاب الناس لذلك الدين

rows.speaker: اليهود
rows.claim: The Jews argue that Moses and the Torah are accepted by consensus, whereas Muhammad's prophethood is not; if the agreed is preferred over the disputed, Judaism should be preferred.
rows.anchor: اليهود قالوا ألستم تقولن إن الأخذ بالمتفق أولى من الأخذ بالمختلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi calls that argument false: Jews accepted Moses because miracles appeared as he claimed, and they witnessed the same kind of miracles confirming Muhammad.
rows.anchor: لأن اليهود أطبقوا على أنه إنما وجب الإيمان بموسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If miracles establish truth, the Jews must acknowledge Muhammad; if they do not, they should not acknowledge Moses. Accepting Moses while rejecting Muhammad despite equivalent miracles is contradictory.
rows.anchor: فإن كان ظهور المعجزة يدل على الصدق ، فههنا يجب الاعتراف بنبوة محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “balance” is the just criterion, the straight scale of equity, accompanying the book that contains kinds of proofs and clear evidences.
rows.anchor: المشتمل على أنواع الدلائل والبينات ، وأنزل الميزان وهو الفصل الذي هو القسطاس المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since people do not know when the Hour will suddenly arrive, a rational person should work hard at inquiry and proof and abandon ignorant imitation.
rows.anchor: وأنهم لا يعلمون أن القيامة متى تفاجئهم ومتى كان الأمر كذلك ، وجب على العاقل أن يجد ويجتهد في النظر والاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mockers ask when the Hour will come and wish it would arrive to show whether their position or Muhammad's is true; the reply is that unbelievers demand it hastily while believers fear it, knowing repentance will then be impossible.
rows.anchor: قالوا على سبيل السخرية : فمتى تقوم القيامة ، وليتها قامت حتى يظهر لنا أن الحق ما نحن عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi glosses mumārāh as argumentative wrangling.
rows.anchor: والممارة الملاجة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that they are people seized by doubt about the Hour, who dispute over it and deny it.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الذين تدخلهم المرية والشك في وقوع الساعة ، فيمارون فيها ويجحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Denying resurrection is far error because justice requires the wronged person's due from the wrongdoer; without resurrection, injustice would be attributed to God, an impossible conclusion.
rows.anchor: لأن استيفاء حق المظلوم من الظالم واجب في العدل ، فلو لم تحصل القيامة لزم إسناد الظلم إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God gentle and kind here is fitting because He sent a book containing subtle proofs and delayed the severe punishment deserved by those who divided.
rows.anchor: لأنه أنزل عليهم الكتاب المشتمل على هذه الدلائل اللطيفة ، فكان ذلك من لطف الله بعباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The postponement of punishment is another kindness, since the divided communities had incurred severe punishment.
rows.anchor: المتفرقون استوجبوا العذاب الشديد ، ثم إنه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's basic beneficence is general: He grants life, intellect, understanding, necessary provision, and protection from most afflictions, though degrees of gifts and joy differ.
rows.anchor: وذلك هو الإحسان بالحياة والعقل والفهم ، وإعطاء ما لا بد منه من الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “Strong” is able to do whatever He wills, and the “Mighty” cannot be overcome or resisted.
rows.anchor: أي القادر على كل ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question could be directed to prophets or unbelievers, but the nearer antecedent is the unbelievers, who admit God created the heavens, earth, and what lies between them.
rows.anchor: فقوله { ولئن سألتهم } يحتمل أن يرجع إلى الأنبياء ، ويحتمل أن يرجع إلى الكفار إلا أن الأقرب رجوعه إلى الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The point is that, despite admitting God is the creator, the polytheists worship others beside Him and deny His power to resurrect.
rows.anchor: والمقصود أنهم مع كونهم مقرين بهذا المعنى يعبدون معه غيره وينكرون قدرته على البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speech then shifts to God describing His own works: idolaters would have said “for us,” not “for you,” and the first-person “We revived” likewise belongs to God's speech.
rows.anchor: لا يتعلق إلا بكلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He illustrates the shift with one speaker naming a mosque's builder and a listener adding further praise: both descriptions concern the same person though they come from different speakers.
rows.anchor: ونظيره من كلام الناس يأن يسمع الرجل رجلا يقول الذي بنى هذا المسجد فلان العالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first divine attribute is creation of the heavens and earth; theologians make the world's origination and God's agency the first proof of God, with “created” understood as bringing into being.
rows.anchor: المتكلمون بينوا أن أول العمل بالله العلم بكونه محدثا للعالم فاعلا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAzīz means overpowering; the capacity for dominance comes from power, so the name signals perfect power.
rows.anchor: العزيز وهو الغالب وما لأجله يحصل المكنة من الغلبة هو القدرة وكان العزيز إشارة إلى كمال القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlīm signals perfect knowledge; together, God's complete knowledge and power mean He can create every possible thing, after which the passage details His works.
rows.anchor: كمال العلم والقدرة إذا حصل كان الموصوف به قادرا على خلق جميع الممكنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth is a resting place because it is stable and has properties that permit cultivation, construction, and concealment of the flaws of living and dead people; like a child's cradle, it offers many comforts.
rows.anchor: كون الأرض مهدا إنما حصل لأجل كونها واقفة ساكنة ولأجل كونها موصوفة بصفات مخصوصة باعتبارها يمكن الانتفاع بها في الزراعة وبناء الأبنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God provides roads so people can travel from town to town and region to region; without the routes and their identifying markers, this benefit would not be possible.
rows.anchor: انتفاع الناس إنما يكمل إذا قدر كل أحد أن يذهب من بلد إلى بلد ومن إقليم إلى إقليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “So that you may be guided” means both that people can find their way along the routes and that they may be guided to religious truth.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى : { لعلكم تهتدون } يعني المقصود من وضع السبل أن يحصل لكم المكنة من الاهتداء ، والثاني المعنى لتهتدوا إلى الحق في الدين

words: وَٱلَّذِى نَزَّلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءًۢ بِقَدَرٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi raises whether rain literally descends from heaven or from clouds, which are called heaven because whatever is elevated is heaven; he says this question was discussed at length earlier.
rows.anchor: ظاهر هذه الآية يقتضي أن الماء ينزل من السماء ، فهل الأمر كذلك أو يقال إنه ينزل من السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain falls in the amount each region needs, neither excess nor shortage, unlike the unmeasured flood sent on Noah's people, and thereby sustains people and livestock.
rows.anchor: إنما ينزل من السماء بقدر ما يحتاج إليه أهل تلك البقعة من غير زيادة ولا نقصان لا كما أنزل على قوم نوح بغير قدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A dead town is one barren of vegetation; God revives it, which is what “spreading life” means here.
rows.anchor: أي خالية من النبات فأحييناها وهو الإنشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reviving dead land demonstrates God's power and wisdom and thus His ability to resurrect people after death, as He revives the earth.
rows.anchor: هذا الدليل كما يدل على قدرة الله وحكمته فكذلك يدل على قدرته على البعث والقيامة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the likeness is that God will recreate and bring people from the earth using water like semen, as rain makes plants grow; Razi calls this weak because the wording only asserts resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم بل وجه التشبيه أن يعيدهم ويخرجهم من الأرض بماء كالمني كما تنبت الأرض بماء المطر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains “pairs” as kinds and varieties, such as sweet and sour, white and black, and male and female.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس الأزاج الضروب والأنواع كالحلو الحامض والأبيض والأسود والذكر والأنثى

rows.speaker: بعض المحققين
rows.claim: Some careful scholars say everything other than God is paired: above and below, directions, past and future, substances and attributes, and the seasons.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المحققين كل ما سوى الله فهو زوج كالفوق والتحت واليمين واليسار والقدام والخلف والماضي والمستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being paired shows that created things are contingent in themselves, originated, and preceded by nonexistence.
rows.anchor: وكونها أزواجا يدل على كونها ممكنة الوجود في ذواتها مخدثة مسبوقة بعدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone is absolutely one, exalted above counterpart, rival, opposite, or helper; the creator of pairs is therefore not Himself paired.
rows.anchor: فأما الحق سبحانه فهو الفرد المنزه عن الشد والند والمقابل والمعاضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arithmetic's first argument for the superiority of the odd or unit: a pair needs two units, whereas the unit is independent of the pair; self-sufficiency is superior to need.
rows.anchor: أن أقل الأزواج هو الإثنان وهو لا يوجد إلا عند ، حصول وحدتين فالزوج يحتاج إلى الفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Second, an even number divides into equal parts while an odd one does not; division is passivity, whereas indivisibility signals strength and resistance.
rows.anchor: الزوج يقبل القسمة بقسمين متساويين والفرد هو الذي لا يقل القسمة وقبول القسمة انفعال وتأثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Third, dividing an odd number yields one even and one odd part, so it contains both types, whereas both halves of an even number are even.
rows.anchor: العدد الفرد لا بد وأن يكون أحد قسميه زوجا والثاني فردا فالعدد الفرد حصل فيه الزوج والفرد معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fourth, paired counterparts share their perfections, so neither is absolutely perfect; the lone one has a perfection exclusive to itself.
rows.anchor: إذا كان كل ما حصل له من الكمال فمثله حاصل لغيره لم يكن هو كاملا على الإطلاق ، أما الفرد فالفردية كائنة له خاصة لا لغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fifth, paired things share some features and differ in others, making each contingent and needy; pairhood is the source of dependence, while oneness is independence and self-sufficiency.
rows.anchor: فكل زوجين فهما ممكنا الوجود لذاتيهما وكل ممكن فهو محتاج فثبت أن الزوجية منشأ الفقر والحاجة

words: وَجَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْفُلْكِ وَٱلْأَنْعَٰمِ مَا تَرْكَبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships carry people on sea journeys and livestock on land journeys.
rows.anchor: السفر إما سفر البحر أو البر ، أما سفر البحر فالحامل هو السفينة ، وأما سفر البر فالحامل هو الأنعام

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains the masculine form through the relative pronoun “what,” with the implied sense “what you ride.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة التذكير لقوله ما والتقدير ما تركبون

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farraʾ says “backs” is plural because it is attributed to a singular collective with plural meaning, as in army or host.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء أضاف الظهور إلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that the feminine is not a true grammatical gender here, so forms may vary, as in “among the women, one who agrees with you.”
rows.anchor: أن هذا التأنيث ليس تأنيثا حقيقيا فجاز أن يختلف اللفظ فيه كما يقال عندي من النساء من يوافقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the direct transitive verb for riding both animals and ships because the construction without a preposition is stronger and therefore predominates.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الجنسين فكيف قال تركبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering the blessing means inwardly recognizing that God created the sea, winds, and ship so a person can steer it in any desired direction; they are not products of human planning, so recognition should lead to obedience and gratitude.
rows.anchor: خلق وجه البحر ، وخلق الرياح ، وخلق جرم السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognizing that God created sea, winds, and ship to answer human steering leads people to submit to Him and thank Him for His endless blessings.
rows.anchor: عرف أن ذلك نعمة عظيمة من الله تعالى ، فيحمله ذلك على الانقياد والطاعة له تعالى ، وعلى الاشتغال بالشكر لنعمه التي لا نهاية لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi lists distinct remembrances for riding a ship, riding livestock, and entering a dwelling: 11:41, 43:13, and 23:29 respectively.
rows.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى عين ذكرا معينا لركوب السفينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A riding animal greatly exceeds a human in strength and lacks reason to guide it in obeying people, yet God made its outer and inner constitution useful to them.
rows.anchor: أكثر قوة من الإنسان بكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Outwardly, the animal's four legs provide a form on which a human can sit securely.
rows.anchor: فلأنها تمشي على أربع قوائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, despite its great strength, God made the animal obedient and subject to humans; contemplating this evokes wonder at divine power and wisdom and the praise in the verse.
rows.anchor: أما خلقها الباطن ، فلأنها مع قوتها الشديدة قد خلقها الله سبحانه بحث تصير منقادة للإنسان ومسخرة له

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses muqrin as one who controls or restrains another.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة : فلان مقرن لفلان ، أي ضابط له

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi derives muqrin from “making a counterpart”; calling oneself another's equal in strength means one can control or match him, and the verse says people lack the power to master ship or beast.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدي : وكان اشتقاقه من قولك ضرب له قرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People lack the strength to match or control a ship or riding animal; God alone subjects them through His knowledge, wisdom, and perfect power.
rows.anchor: فكان المعنى أنه ليس عندنا من القوة والطاقة أن نقرن هذه الدابة والفلك وأن نضبطها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The report in al-Kashshaf says the Prophet said “In God's name” when putting his feet in the stirrup, then praised God and recited the subjugation remembrance after mounting.
rows.anchor: روى صاحب ( الكشفا ) : عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الحسن بن علي
rows.claim: Abu Makhlad reports that al-Hasan ibn Ali saw a man mount an animal and said, “Glory to Him who favored us with Muhammad,” praised God for making them the best community, then recited the riding remembrance.
rows.anchor: روى القاضي في ( تفسيره ) : عن أبي مخلد أن الحسن بن علي عليهما السلام : رأى رجلا ركب دابة ، فقال سبحان الذي من علينا بمحمد

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: A report says that on a journey the Messenger said takbir three times, recited the riding remembrance, prayed for righteousness, piety, pleasing deeds, an easy journey, God's companionship, and care for his family; returning, he said they were returning repentant and praising God.
rows.anchor: وروي أيضا عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أنه كان إذا سافر وركب راحلته ، كبر ثلاثا

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf argues that the purpose clause shows God intended people to mount and remember Him, contradicting the Mujabbira claim that He intended unbelief and persistence in denial.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب ( الكشاف ) : دلت هذه الآية على خلاف قول المجبرة من وجوه الأول : أنه تعالى قال : { لتستووا على ظهوره ثم تذكروا نعمة ربكم

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: A second argument against the Mujabbira is that the purpose clause “so that you may settle” shows God's action is directed toward ends.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن قوله { لتستووا } يدل على أن فعله معلل بالأغراض

rows.speaker: صاحب الكشاف
rows.claim: A third argument says God created animals with these traits so servants would give thanks; if human acts were God's acts, this would mean He created the animals to create the phrase on a servant's tongue, though He could create the phrase without those means.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه تعالى بين أن خلق هذه الحيوانات على هذه الطبائع إنما كان لغرض أن يصدر الشكر على العبد
